incident-bot: :warning: 06:10 UTC - Elevated GPU OOMs during prefill detected in pool `gpu-prod-us-west-2`. Restart storms observed on several containers. Auto-raise to #incidents.

sre_jordan: I'm up. pulling logs now. which nodes?

oncall_maya: nodes ip-10-0-22{7,8,9} reporting repeated container restarts. dmesg indicates `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1): 31` and driver resets.

eng-runtime-anna: quick summary from runtime traces: prefill path is allocating huge KV segments for some requests with single-shot contexts > 50k tokens. The memory spike happens before token generation starts. stack excerpt: ```Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/svc/runtime/handler.py", line 412, in handle_request
    prefill_result = runner.prefill(request.tokens)
  File "/svc/runtime/prefill.py", line 274, in prefill
    self.kv_cache.grow(estimated_size)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.10 GiB```

support-luca: logged customer incidents: 6 reports in the last 20m. Two are higher-tier customers doing bulk transcript ingestion (huge prompts). They see 500s and timeouts.

possible fix idea: server-side limiting + best-effort prompt compression + fallback to CPU/cold-model.

eng-runtime-anna: proposed immediate mitigations:
- push a temporary server-side guard: reject/pause/trim requests with prefill token estimate > 12k (config: `runtime.prefill.soft_limit_tokens`)
- enable a prefill-memory-safety-check that rejects allocations > 2GiB before committing
- roll a runtime flag to swap large contexts into a cold-model process (CPU-backed) rather than attempting GPU prefill
- lower pod concurrency on affected daemonset from 4 -> 1 to reduce simultaneous peaks

sre_jordan: initiate hot-fix: setting `runtime.prefill.soft_limit_tokens=12288` for a canary subset (label: prefill-hotfix=true). will route 5% traffic. deploy-bot, please start rollout.

deploy-bot: Rollout initiated by sre_jordan at 06:14 UTC. Canary: 4 pods. Auto-rollback on >3 restarts per pod in 5m.

oncall_maya: running `kubectl set env deploy/runtime-gpu -n prod runtime_prefill_soft_limit_tokens=12288 --selector=prefill-hotfix=true`. tailing output.

eng-runtime-anna: config pushed to canary includes: ```yaml
runtime:
  prefill:
    soft_limit_tokens: 12288
    trim_strategy: head_tail
  fallback:
    cold_model_enabled: true
    cold_model_threshold_gb: 1.5
```

support-luca: immediate observation: canary nodes stopped restarting within ~60s. non-canary still flapping. should we move affected enterprise tenants to canary? they reported degraded UX but prefer stability.

pm-elaine: coordinate moving two enterprise tenants to canary routing now. get approval from security if needed?

sre_jordan: routing change applied for tenant-42 and tenant-88 via traffic-override. confirming connection.

incident-bot: Metrics snapshot (06:18 UTC): prefill OOM rate on canary: 0.2/min, non-canary: 15/min. Cluster restarts reduced by 18% after canary.

eng-runtime-anna: next steps if canary stable for 8m: expand hotfix to 50% then 100%. also will raise a PR to add proactive token-estimation earlier in request pipeline to short-circuit extreme requests (PR 6814). Need a follow-on to investigate allocator behavior that allows temporary peaks above configured cache sizes.

support-luca: customer-impact note: 6 customers affected; two enterprise had 5xx for approx 8-10 minutes until we routed them. Recommend sending a brief status email and offer extra support.

oncall_maya: adding temporary alert suppression for nodes under active remediation so we don't page on each restart. slack: #incidents will still get updates.

sre_jordan: canary looks good after 9m. expanding to 50% now. starting gradual rollout.

deploy-bot: Canary -> 50% started at 06:23 UTC. Auto-rollback on threshold.

eng-runtime-anna: check: we'll also enable a KV cache eviction policy during rollout: LRU entries older than 20m will be evicted to bound growth. this should reduce long-term steady-state memory.

incident-bot: Update (06:26 UTC): OOMs dropping cluster-wide as rollout progresses. Affected enterprise tenants now routed to stable instances. No customer data corruption reported.

pm-elaine: please prepare a short public-facing blurb: cause (large single-request contexts causing GPU OOMs during prefill), impact (some customers saw 500s, two enterprise briefly affected), mitigation (hotfix limiting prefill tokens + routing + fallback).

support-luca: drafting message and will share with pm-elaine for review.

oncall_maya: handing off monitoring to next oncall in 25m. summary attached to shift notes.

eng-runtime-anna: preliminary root cause hypothesis: unbounded KV cache growth for extreme prefill sizes combined with a recent GPU kernel change that increased temporary workspace usage produced peak allocations beyond GPU capacity. working on a reproducer and unit tests.

- eng-runtime (anna): add prefill estimator + add allocation cap + unit tests (owner: anna)
- eng-runtime (anna) & infra: audit recent kernel optimizer changes (owner: anna, infra)
- sre (jordan): schedule driver/firmware upgrade window for nodes that saw repeated resets
- support (luca): finalize customer comms and log ticket references
